## Historical audit — S0160

**Scope:** Visible chunk 1 of 2 only. All citations below refer to S0160, original file `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/sceneevolve_cli/C2/selection/commons_138420790/trajectory.jsonl`. The supplied observations contain no image pixels for independent inspection.

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| Student request, line 1 | The explicit goal was reconstruction of one indoor RGB scene with separate editable meshes, inferred camera and materials, without reference projection or additional views. |
| Student response and execution, lines 3–5 | The student described a kitchen and built multiple grouped assets: architecture, posts, rear cabinetry and ovens, an island with drawers, sink and faucet, hood, and kettle. The code specifies colors, procedural timber grain, a camera and lights. Multipart grouping is observable; physical connections and visual fidelity are not independently verified. Step 1 executed successfully and the runner saved a render and blend file. |
| Student audit, lines 8–10 | The student received the step-1 result and image paths, then *reported* low framing, excessive post occlusion and gray cabinetry/pale timber. It hypothesized coupled camera/post and material causes and proposed specific changes. These are student visual judgments, not independent measurements. |
| Revision and result, lines 14, 16–17 | Step 2 changed camera position and shift, moved and narrowed the post, and darkened materials while retaining lights and principal object dimensions. Execution returned `ok: true` and saved a render. This is actual adoption of the student’s own audit, not evidence of teacher input. |
| Second audit and revision, lines 22, 24–25 | The student reported a broad pale wall in step 2, shallow island-end perspective, and still-light timber and cabinetry. Step 3 moved the wall, changed camera and post placement, darkened surfaces and explicitly assigned procedural grain. It also executed successfully and saved a render. These changes test the student’s hypotheses; their effectiveness is unverified here. |
| Selection events and last visible request, lines 18–19, 23, 26–28 | Selection events alternated between newly executed steps and fallback step 1. The last visible request asks the student to select among all three renders; its response is not in this chunk. No final selection or formal task-success verdict is visible. |

**Teacher and autonomy.** No teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or teacher input is visible in this chunk, and no teacher adoption can be established. The student performed iterative, model-only visual comparison and revisions under prompted constraints; session records report zero tool calls within the student CLI sessions (lines 2, 9, 13, 21). The runner, rather than the student program, executed and rendered the builds.

**Outcome and lessons.** Three nonempty builds formally executed without reported errors; this establishes technical execution, not reconstruction correctness. Final outcome remains **unknown**, rather than an algorithm failure or technical interruption. A transferable observation is that the student separated camera/occlusion hypotheses from material/light hypotheses and preserved a fallback while testing revisions. The particular wall, post, and timber corrections are scene-specific hypotheses. Whether meshes actually meet cleanly, the static objects’ spatial pose and occlusions match the photograph, textures were assigned as intended, or lighting and framing improved remains unresolved without inspecting the images and the unseen continuation.
